summary: Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. His career includes serving as Lecturer and Co-Director at the University of Bristol and President of the Pali Text Society.
A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Ruriko Sakuma studied at Nagoya University. Her appointments include serving as a researcher and director at the Eastern Institute, attested in 2015.
Rustam Sabirov works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned a doctorate in history from Moscow State University in 2004 and later served there as a Senior Researcher.

Working in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Ruth Fuller Sasaki studied at the University of Chicago and under D.T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She directed the Buddhist Society of America and served as abbess of Ryosen-an.

Ruth Gamble specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, completing her Ph.D. at the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She held posts at the University of Munich and the Australian National University.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis.

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, D. Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, and several traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brown and Harvard, later holding posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley, and Wesleyan University.
Ryōshō Taira was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Taisho University, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 1976 and attested again in 1984.
Ryodo Kudo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held positions as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Ryūjō Yamada and Ryotai Hatani, and also at Humboldt University of Berlin. He lectured at Humboldt and was a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1953 to 1978.
Ryoichi Kondo was a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career included serving as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Ryokei Kaginushi worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career included serving as a professor in the Faculty of Letters and university professor at Otani University, attested between 1978 and 1993.

Ryoko Mochizuki works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo from circa 1957 to 1963, she held appointments as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1972 and 1983.
Ryomin Akizuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1941 to 1944 and held a post at Saitama Medical University around 1972.

Ryosaburo Sakaki specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, subsequently lecturing at Ryukoku University and serving as professor at Third Higher School and Kyoto University.

Ryosei Fuji works in Buddhist studies. After studying at Dongguk University, he held posts at Daegu University, the Institute for Religious Culture, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo, and Ryukoku University.

Ryosei Fukuda specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Toyo University. He served as professor and professor emeritus at Taisho University, head of Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies, and held positions at Chisan Denpōin, Chisan Senshū Gakuin, and Shuchiin University.
